title: quickfire-ops-checkpoint-announce-scratch-oliver
content:
TL;DR: Quick midweek ops checkpoint to surface capacity headroom, lingering incidents, and an ask for lightweight triage support. Intended for short company broadcast plus an optional 15-min sync for product leads.

Audience: engineering, product leads, support on-call rotation, and customer-facing SRE liaisons. Not a full postmortem — this is a rapid situational note and a request for short-term help.

Channel suggestions:
- Short post on #company-sync (preview + link to doc)
- Optional 15-min quick sync: Thursday 11:00 (calendar invite if >5 RSVPs)

Purpose:
- Keep the org aware of where we're at with capacity and degraded subsystems (avoid surprise escalation)
- Get quick alignment on feature throttles and temporary routing rules for tomorrow's peak window
- Surface two small asks that need ~2-3 people each for ~2 hours of focused work

Proposed micro-script (for PM/lead to read or paste in channel):
"Hey folks — quick ops checkpoint: we have headroom but two things to be aware of ahead of tomorrow's midday peak. 1) Persistent error tail on small subset of dedicated pods (trace id range 0x7a–0x9f) that increases 1–2% p50 request latency when concurrent KV cache warm-ups happen. 2) A routing misconfiguration that could route low-priority batch jobs to the reserved pool during autoscale events. We're asking for a short sync if you want to join, and a couple of hands to triage the two items below. Details here: <doc link>"

Quick state (what we know):
- Capacity: Dedicated pools at 72% nominal utilization; buffer configured for 80% before autoscale. Short-term headroom ok but low on some AZs (eu-west-1b) — cross-AZ burst likely to trigger cold-starts.
- Incident tail: Starting 2026-02-20 noticed intermittent 503s on model-serving v2.1 when KV misses + long seq lengths coincide. Root cause likely cache eviction contention in runtime.
- Routing: Canary policy for small-batch reroute mistakenly includes a label used by reserve pool tagging; leads to 3–6% of batch jobs landing on reserve pool under specific patterns.

Asks (concrete, time-boxed):
1) Runtime triage: 2 engineers (serving-runtime) for 2 hours to collect flamegraphs and replicate with longer sequence workloads (A/B test reproducer attached). Target: narrow to eviction hotspot or confirm kernel regression.
2) Policy fix + short rollback: 1 engineer (platform) to update canary routing label filter and push a 30-min rollback job to validate over the next 24 hours.
3) Monitoring tweak (low effort): 1 engineer (observability) to add short-lived alert that fires when reserve-pool allocation >5% of batch traffic.

Anticipated Qs & suggested answers:
- Q: Is customer traffic impacted? A: A small fraction (<0.5%) of requests may see higher latency or 503; no major customer-facing degradation tracked so far. We’re monitoring.
- Q: Why didn't autoscaling handle it? A: Autoscale thresholds are based on aggregated GPU util; the issue is eviction contention causing request tail rather than sustained util spike. Autoscale is orthogonal.
- Q: Risk of rollback? A: Minimal — the label filter change and short rollback only affect routing for batch jobs and can be reverted within a single deploy window.

Notes to sender (internal):
- Keep the public wording non-technical; link to this doc for deeper details.
- Do not mention internal incident IDs or customer PIDs in the broadcast. Use placeholders and attach the sensitive logs only in the private slack thread.
- If execs ask for immediate postmortem, we will provide a high-level timeline and commit to a 5-business-day postmortem if the issue escalates.

Fallback talking points (if asked live):
- "We're actively triaging with runtime and platform engineers; initial mitigations cut the error rate in half in our test runs."
- "No rollback of user-facing changes planned — this is a routing/policy fix + runtime investigation."

Open items / TODOs:
- [ ] Schedule 15-min sync (owner: Oliver)
- [ ] Assign runtime leads for reproducer (owner: Mina)
- [ ] Platform engineer to patch label filter and run canary (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Observability quick alert (owner: SRE-oncall)

Attachments & artifacts (for private thread):
- reproducer.tar.gz (seq-len 2048)
- flamegraph snapshots (private link)
- routing-policy-diff (PR link)

Version notes: this is a scratch draft. If we get buy-in, we will convert to a short PR/announcement with a one-paragraph summary and the private quick-links.

[END OF DRAFT]

Inline notes for later edits:
- Make script <140 chars for broadcast headline.
- Consider adding a single customer-impact sentence if SRE confirms >1% user impact.
- If sync has >10 RSVPs, convert to 30-min and add ops lead to agenda."
